messages.subject: Covariates in scanone/scantwo
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

    How are covariates with more than two levels treated in scanone and
scantwo?  In my case, I have 4 levels that represent an continuous
gradient.  Because they are forced to be a number in scanone, I suspect
that they are treated as.numeric in the model.  However, I know suspect
that there are non-linear effects of the QTL from running scanone within
each environment.  Thus, I would like to be able to treat my covariate
as a factor.  Is this possible?

Thanks,
Alan

messages.subject: Re: Covariates in scanone/scantwo
messages.body_plain:
If you have a 4-level factor as a covariate, you need to
explicitly code the 3 covariate columns for your model.

If "f" is the factor, you might write:

   x <- as.numeric(f)
   m <- matrix(0, ncol=length(levels(f))-1, nrow=length(f))
   for(i in 1:(length(levels(f))-1))
     m[x==i,i] <- 1

Then use the "m" matrix as the covariate.

karl

messages.subject: Re: Covariates in scanone/scantwo
messages.body_plain:
You can.  All of the covariates in scanone() and scantwo()
must be strictly numeric.  You can make a single column, or
you can expand it to several columns, but the expansion is
not yet done automatically.

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.03-14
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.03-14) has been released at its web site
(http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl).

See http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl/STATUS.txt for a list of
changes.  The major changes are listed below.

I've also added two things to the R/qtl web site: a page with sample
data files and and code for importing the files into R, and a list of
frequently asked questions.

As always, I'd appreciate hearing any suggestions or comments or
complaints.

Karl Broman
kbr...@jhsph.edu

------

Major changes in R/qtl version 1.03-14:

  Fixed subset.cross() so that the attribitutes in the results of
  calc.genoprob, calc.errorlod, sim.geno, and argmax.geno, don't get
  lost on subsetting.  This was important to ensure that the package
  will conform to a change that will occur in the next release of R.

  Added a function checkAlleles() for identifying loci that might have
  their alleles switched (in an intercross, if AA and BB are switched,
  or in a backcross if AA and AB are switched).  The X chromosome is
  ignored.  An internal function, checkrf() was removed; this was
  previously called by est.rf() but wasn't well written.

  Added an argument, alleles, for read.cross(), which takes two
  single-character allele labels that are included as an attribute in
  the cross and will be used as labels throughout the program (for
  example, in geno.table, effectplot and plot.pxg).  This required
  numerous small changes throughout the package.

  The maps used for the results from argmax.geno(), calc.genoprob()
  and sim.geno() are now saved as an attribute on the data they
  create (within the cross object) so that create.map() doesn't have
  to be called repeatedly.

  Moved the code for simulating genotype data in sim.cross() into C,
  to increase speed, and modified it so that one may simulate under
  Frank Stahl's interference model (which includes the chi-square
  model as a special case).

  If one includes a phenotype named "id" or "ID", this will be used in
  top.errorlod(), plot.errorlod(), and plot.geno() as identifiers for
  the individual.

messages.body_plain:

point; there's generally not room for them down there.

purposes.

to allow this.  I'll add it to my (rather long) list of things to do.

karl

messages.subject: Scantwo plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

Is it possible to make the font smaller for the chromosome numbers on a
scantwo plot?  Even with the figure fully enlarged, some of the numbers
still run together.

Thanks,
Abby
messages.body_snippet:

still run together.

messages.subject: Re: Scantwo plot
messages.body_plain:
They can be modified only by going into the code for plot.scantwo and
editing things directly.

Create a copy of the plot.scantwo.R file from the source code, and
find the following lines:

     # add chromesome numbers
     a <- par("usr")
     for(i in 1:length(n.mar)) {
       text(mean(wh[i + c(0, 1)]), a[3] - diff(a[3:4]) * 0.025,
            chr[i], xpd = TRUE, adj = c(0.5, 1))
       segments(mean(wh[i + c(0, 1)]), a[3],
                mean(wh[i + c(0, 1)]), a[3] - diff(a[3:4]) * 0.01,
xpd = TRUE)
       text(a[1] - diff(a[1:2]) * 0.025, mean(wh[i + c(0, 1)]),
            chr[i], xpd = TRUE, adj = c(1, 0.5))
       segments(a[1], mean(wh[i + c(0, 1)]), a[1] - diff(a[1:2]) *
                0.01, mean(wh[i + c(0, 1)]), xpd = TRUE)
     }

In the text() lines, add something like cex=0.8, where the number
controls the size of the text.

If you load this into R using source(), it will be used in place of
the built-in plot.scantwo function.

karl
